fields.position: Share query-only SID prefixes planned by 7B and complete them with a 0.5B model under current history; ReuseCut chooses depth through sequential coverage criteria.
fields.tradeoff: Retains more personalization than caching final results, but deeper reuse restricts reachability. Prepared depth zero and cold misses use different models; a label kernel is not learned BudgetCut.

fields.position: Business-weight BPE merges and apply a bounded parent-rank sigmoid bonus when pruning free-text query generations.
fields.tradeoff: Differs from fixed-SID subtree constraints and LCP penalties. Rank bonuses measure no pairwise semantic distance and do not unconditionally preserve final top-1. STAR, MARS-DPO and the full query model are not implemented locally.

fields.title: Shared computation, output objects and candidate diversification are separate decisions
fields.body: TIGER turns items into semantic-code paths. ReuseGR retains SID hierarchy but shares query-prefix planning across users while current history still affects suffixes. SPADE instead generates executable free-text queries: OA-BPE changes tokenization priors, then parent-rank bonuses affect search survival; this is not PinGER common-SID-prefix penalization. Fix candidate budgets and output objects before comparing history-input, offline-planning and online-decoding costs. Reachable prefix coverage is not complete retrieval improvement.

fields.question: Can ReuseGR, PinGER and SPADE be reduced to one prefix/diversity score?
fields.answer: Not without preserving their distinctions. ReuseGR controls reuse depth and reachable subtrees; PinGER penalizes repeated common-SID-prefix subtrees; SPADE rewards parent rank while producing free-text queries. They act on different objects and stages. Align serving budgets before separately evaluating reachability, redundancy and final quality.
fields.example: Teaching example: Caching two prefix levels saves computation but need not diversify candidates. Rewarding a lower-ranked free-text query does not calculate its semantic distance from already selected queries.

fields.summary: Adds ReuseGR and SPADE, distinguishing query-prefix reuse, user-history conditioning, business-tokenization priors and parent-rank bonuses against TIGER/PinGER. Output objects and budgets remain explicit; CPU operators and full-system A/B are different evidence tiers.

fields.position: One autoregressive policy unifies reranking and mix-ranking, with RMs used only offline; decoding retains hard masks and finite adjustments, while RM and rule rewards are standardized separately.
fields.tradeoff: Geometric rewards and ensemble penalties are proxies, not guarantees for every business metric. Local rules do not guarantee global feasibility. Local delivery is CPU constraint/arithmetic reference code, not trained slate models.

fields.title: A unified slate policy still separates hard constraints from proxy rewards
fields.body: CDM distills marginal slate supervision from a controlled MMR teacher. OneTrans-GSR instead uses slate RMs to guide one policy that directly generates mixed-content sequences. Its geometric objective first applies group min-max normalization and a positive floor, while rule rewards require separate standardization; it is not arbitrary multiplication of business scores. Hard masks prevent forbidden actions, finite penalties permit trade-offs, and local quotas may conflict. Record RM proxy scores, final selection and real A/B separately rather than relabel CPU arithmetic or predictions on unexposed slates as user gains.

fields.question: Does OneTrans-GSR geometric reward guarantee that no objective deteriorates?
fields.answer: No. Flooring and geometric aggregation change proxy trade-offs, not prove Pareto improvement; a constant objective contributes the same group factor. Actual user effects require independent production A/B, and passing local masks does not prove a jointly feasible completion.
fields.example: Teaching example: Multiplying normalized click and GMV proxies can still favor a slate overestimated by the RM. A higher CPU formula score is not additional orders.

fields.summary: Adds OneTrans-GSR, separating single-policy slate generation, offline RM proxies, geometric objectives and independent standardization. The comparison with CDM keeps teacher/policy differences explicit; local constraints and online evidence are not substitutes.
